text:
incident-bot: PAGING: Elevated 5xxs on inference-gateway-private (eu-west-1). 5xx rate 4.3% over 5m window, threshold 1%. See /runbooks/private-egress-nat.
amelia: ugh, hitting the on-call list. @network_oncall @sre_lead can you pick this up? Customers on private peering reporting 504s/timeouts.
network_oncall: on it, looking at peering metrics + bgp. grabbing flow logs and nat metrics.
sre_lead: Amelia — which tenants are impacted? any customer-facing SEs alerted?
karen_support: We have three paying customers reporting errors: AcmeAI (enterprise), DataSage (mid-market), and an internal smoke test service (redwood-eval). All show repeated 504s on model request paths. I've DM'd customer-sre to get traces.
customer-sre: Confirmed tcp timeouts from AcmeAI to inference-gateway IPs via their VPC peering. They see SYN then no ACK from upstream.
dheeraj: Pulling NAT metrics: nat-gw-priv-01 shows high ephemeral port churn and conntrack near capacity. snippet from metrics: 
```
nat_ephemeral_used: 64321/65536
nf_conntrack_count: 258900/262144
5xx_rate: 4.3%
avg_latency: 810ms
```
This smells like ephemeral port depletion + conntrack pressure.
network_oncall: BGP graphs show occasional route withdraws for the peering prefix at 10:12:17 UTC, short flaps lasting ~3-8s, then traffic re-routed to the same nat. Could be triggering ephemeral reuse and asymmetric return paths.
sre_lead: Action plan: 1) reduce customer impact ASAP by creating fallback routing to alternate nat/gw, 2) expand ephemeral pool / conntrack as immediate mitigation, 3) investigate root cause (peering flaps) for postmortem. Who can make the route change?
amelia: @ops-bot can we run a weighted route change to prefer nat-gw-priv-02 for the affected prefixes? Need canary first for AcmeAI then global.
ops-bot: Received cla request. Please confirm target prefix list and weight.
network_oncall: Target prefixes: acct-acmeai-10.0.0.0/22, acct-datasage-10.4.0.0/22, redwood-eval-10.8.0.0/24. Set weight to prefer nat-gw-priv-02 (weight +100) for those prefixes. I'll apply in one minute.
network_oncall: Applying route weight change now -> `apply-route-weight --prefix acct-acmeai-10.0.0.0/22 --prefer nat-gw-priv-02 --delta 100`
ops-bot: Route change applied. BGP advertisement updated.
dheeraj: While route change propagates, I'm bumping conntrack and ephemeral range on nat-gw-priv-01 as emergency mitigation:
```
echo 524288 > /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="15000 61000"
```
Doing that now.
network_oncall: Bump done on nat-gw-priv-01 and nat-gw-priv-02. Conntrack headroom increased.
amelia: Monitoring application error rates and customer pings now.
incident-bot: METRIC UPDATE (3m): 5xx rate down to 1.8% on inference-gateway-private. Latency median improved to 420ms.
karen_support: AcmeAI: reports API success rate back to normal for a few minutes, then intermittent spikes. DataSage similar. They're asking what changed.
sre_lead: Noted. We did weighted route preference + conntrack/ephemeral bump. Need to keep an eye for recurrence.
dheeraj: I also saw high conntrack timeout values for a bunch of stale entries from the peer ASN. Reduced conntrack timeout for ESTABLISHED to 60s to free table faster: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=60`
network_oncall: BGP flaps still visible but less frequent. Looks like remote transit may be re-advertising alternate path causing asymmetric SNAT. I'm collecting bgp logs to correlate with timestamps on 504 spikes.
customer-sre: AcmeAI sent us pcap — observed SYN->SYN-ACK sometimes taking alternate path and hitting a different NAT instance which didn't have the right ephemeral mapping, resulting in 5xx from gateway.
sre_lead: That confirms asymmetric return path + ephemeral reuse -> connection resets. For medium-term mitigation: request peering partner to stabilize route selection or add more deterministic next-hop via BGP community (no-policy). Also prepare NAT affinity / deterministic SNAT (source port persistence) for private peering.
amelia: I'm drafting a status note to impacted customers summarizing mitigations and next steps. @karen_support can you send interim message?
karen_support: Drafted: "We've applied emergency routing changes and increased NAT/conntrack capacity to mitigate 5xxs. We're investigating peering instability as root cause and will follow up with a permanent fix." Sending now.
ops-bot: Customer notifications dispatched to AcmeAI and DataSage points of contact.
incident-bot: METRIC UPDATE (9m): 5xx rate now 0.9% (below threshold). Continued monitoring for 30m.
network_oncall: Planning follow-ups: 1) Engage transit partner on BGP stability, 2) schedule controlled rollback of conntrack/tuning during maintenance window, 3) design deterministic SNAT for private peers.
dheeraj: I'll open an infra ticket to add NAT autoscaling and deterministic port allocation per peer (INFRA-5732). Also adding more aggressive conntrack GC and reducing ESTABLISHED timeout back when safe.
sre_lead: Great. I'll take ownership of the postmortem and action list. Amelia, leave a short handoff for next oncall.
amelia: Handoff to next oncall @network_oncall at 3012345940. Notes: emergency route pref to nat-gw-priv-02 applied, conntrack/ephemeral range bumped, ESTABLISHED timeout reduced. Customers notified. Investigate BGP flaps and build deterministic SNAT.
network_oncall: Acknowledged. I'll follow with bgp logs and diff of route advertisements.
incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. Creating incident record INC-3012345678.
ops-bot: On-call escalation completed. Next update scheduled +30m.
amelia: Thanks all. Leaving channel for now.
network_oncall: closing loop: 5xxs stable <1% for 15m. will keep monitoring and escalate if it creeps.
project-note: postmortem owner=sre_lead; followups=[engage-transit, deterministic-snat, nat-autoscale, improved-metrics]; sev=high; customer-impact=AcmeAI, DataSage; incident-duration=~35m
